transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you lately and why you've come in today?

Well, I came in because... I mean, things have been a little weird lately. I've started doing things at work—I'm a bookkeeping clerk, you know, mostly handling receipts and invoices—and at school that just don't make sense. Like, I'll take all the receipts and just start lining them up across the floor. Which reminds me, the floors at my office are this awful beige tile, the kind that always looks dirty even right after the janitor mops it. He uses this pine cleaner that smells so strong it gives me a headache. But anyway, yeah, I've been doing things like tapping the calculator in sets of nine. Nine taps, exactly. And sometimes I'll just stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air, just standing there until someone walks by and asks if I'm okay. The copier is always jamming anyway, especially when you try to use the legal-size paper. I don't know why we even buy that paper, nobody uses it except for the tax forms, and those are mostly digital now anyway. So yeah, that's why I'm here.
Do you feel anxious or upset if you can't complete these actions, like tapping the calculator nine times or arranging receipts?

Anxious? Um... no, I don't really think so. I haven't really noticed feeling upset if I don't finish it or if someone stops me. Like, if someone interrupts me, it's just... whatever. Speaking of being interrupted, Mr. Henderson—he's the office manager—he came up to my desk yesterday while I was doing the receipt thing. He always wears these really loud, obnoxious ties. Yesterday it was bright yellow with little cartoon golf clubs all over it. Which is weird because I'm pretty sure he doesn't even play golf. He spends all his weekends working on his truck. It's one of those massive lifted trucks that takes up two spaces in the lot. It drives everyone crazy because our parking lot is tiny, and it's shared with this deli next door. They make a really good turkey club sandwich, but you have to tell them like three times to go easy on the mayo, otherwise they just drown the bread in it. It gets so soggy by the time you bring it back to your desk, and I hate soggy bread. But anyway, what was I... oh, yeah, no, I don't really get mad or anxious about the tapping or anything.
Do you find yourself having thoughts or worries that won't go away and that might be causing you to do these things with the receipts or the calculator?

Thoughts or worries? Hmm... no, not really. I mean, my head isn't filled with any specific worries that make me want to line up the receipts or anything. It's not like I'm sitting there stressing about things. But speaking of stressing, my mom has been so stressed lately about her garden. She planted all these tomatoes this year, the heirloom kind, you know? But the squirrels keep getting to them right before they ripen. She tried putting up this chicken wire fence, but those squirrels are like acrobats. I saw one literally launch itself from the oak tree branch, do a flip, and land right on top of a tomato plant. It was crazy. The oak tree is huge, by the way, it drops acorns everywhere in the fall, and if you step on them just right, you can twist your ankle. My brother actually did that last year right before his prom. He had to wear this clunky walking boot with his tuxedo, which looked ridiculous because his tux was navy blue and the boot was bright gray. He rented the tux from this place downtown that always smells like mothballs and old carpet. But yeah, no, I don't have any stuck thoughts or worries making me do that stuff.

Do you feel like you have to do these things—like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator—a certain number of times to make something bad from happening, or to make yourself feel better in some way?

Make something bad from happening? No, I don't think so. I don't feel like... like I'm preventing a disaster or anything. It's just something I do. But talking about disasters, you should have seen the breakroom yesterday. Someone left a tuna casserole in the microwave for way too long. It basically exploded. The smell was just... it was everywhere. It seeped out into the hallway and even into the lobby. The receptionist, Brenda, she was so mad because she had this big meeting with a vendor coming in, and the whole place smelled like burnt fish. Brenda is always super particular about how the lobby looks and smells. She buys these expensive candles, the ones that cost like thirty dollars for a tiny jar, and burns them all day. Her favorite is this lavender and cedarwood one. She says it's calming, but honestly, it just smells like my grandmother's attic. My grandmother had this huge collection of porcelain dolls up there. Hundreds of them. They had those creepy glass eyes that seemed to follow you when you walked around the room. I hated going up there when I was a kid. But yeah, to answer your question, no, I don't do the tapping or the receipts to stop anything bad from happening or to feel better.
Do you ever have intrusive, unwanted thoughts that pop into your mind that make you feel uncomfortable, like thoughts about contamination, harm, or needing things to be perfectly ordered?

Unwanted thoughts? Um, no, not really. I don't get thoughts like that popping into my head, like about germs or things needing to be perfect. I mean, I like things neat, but it's not like an uncomfortable thought that forces me to do it. Speaking of germs, though, you wouldn't believe how much hand sanitizer Brenda goes through at the front desk. She buys it by the gallon, I swear. It's that kind that smells really strongly of fake aloe vera, you know? Like, it doesn't smell like a plant at all, it just smells like chemicals. It reminds me of the pool I used to go to when I was a kid, the community one over on 5th Street. They put so much chlorine in that water, your eyes would burn if you even opened them for a second underwater. We used to have these diving rings, the plastic ones that sink to the bottom, and we'd have competitions to see who could grab the most in one breath. My buddy Mark was always the best at it because he had huge lungs. He played the tuba in the marching band, which makes sense, right? You need a lot of air for that. The tuba is so heavy, though. He had to wear this special harness thing just to carry it during the parades. The parades in our town are always on the hottest days of the summer, too, so the asphalt is literally melting your shoes. But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the thoughts. No, I don't really have any of those uncomfortable, unwanted thoughts.
Have you ever felt driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts over and over again, even if you didn't want to, because you felt like you had to?

Driven to do things over and over... no, I don't feel forced to do anything like that. I mean, I do things because I want to, not because I have to. It's not like a compulsion or anything. But speaking of doing things over and over, you should see the way my boss reviews the ledgers. He literally checks the same column of numbers like five times. It's exhausting just watching him. He uses this red pen, always a red pen, and he makes these tiny little checkmarks next to every single entry. He buys those pens in bulk from this office supply store that's going out of business. The whole store has these big yellow signs in the windows saying "Everything Must Go!" but they've been up for like six months. I don't know how they're still open. They sell these really cheap desk chairs, too, the ones where the wheels always get stuck on the carpet. My chair at work has a stuck wheel, and every time I try to scoot over to the filing cabinet, I end up dragging it and making this awful scraping noise. It drives the lady in the cubicle next to me crazy. She's always listening to classical music on her headphones to drown out the office noise. She says Mozart helps her concentrate, but I don't know, all those violins just make me feel sleepy. Especially right after lunch. But yeah, no, I don't feel driven to do things over and over like I'm forced to.
Have you ever noticed any unusual sensory experiences, like hearing voices when no one is around, seeing things that others don't see, or feeling sensations on your skin with no clear cause?

Hearing things? Um, well, sometimes, yeah. Like, if I'm just sitting alone at my desk at work, or maybe walking home from class, I'll hear this man's voice. It's super clear, like he's standing right next to me. He'll say something like "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." I always look around, but there's literally nobody there. 

It's weird because line seven on our main office ledger is usually the accounts receivable from this one specific client, Henderson Auto. They always pay late. Like, thirty days net means absolutely nothing to them. They still send physical checks in the mail, too, and the envelopes always have this weird blue watermark on them. I asked the mailroom guy about it once. His name is Dave, and Dave collects stamps, so he knows all about that kind of paper stuff. He has this huge leather binder of stamps from all over the world, even places that don't exist anymore, like the Soviet Union or whatever. He showed me this one stamp that had a tiny printing error on the airplane's wing, and apparently, it's worth like two thousand dollars. Can you imagine carrying around a tiny piece of paper worth that much? I'd be terrified of dropping it in a puddle. 

The puddles on my walk home are getting ridiculous, by the way, because the city has been doing construction on 4th Street for what feels like a decade. They just leave those big orange barrels everywhere, and the water just pools up around them. Some guy drove through one yesterday and splashed water all over the sidewalk. But anyway, yeah, I'll hear that guy's voice telling me to check line seven or that I missed a sign, even when I'm completely by myself.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn't seem to understand or agree with, even though you felt certain it was true?

Believed something strongly... yeah, actually. I know it sounds strange, but at work, I get completely convinced that certain invoice totals, or like, specific account numbers and due dates are actually messages about me. Like they're put there specifically for me to read. My supervisor will sit down with me and pull up the ledgers to show me they're just normal entries. He uses this really old accounting software, by the way, it's from like 2010 or something. The whole interface is just this depressing gray and neon green. It totally looks like the code falling in The Matrix, you know? Have you seen that movie? 

The first one is a classic, but the sequels get so confusing. My buddy Mark, the tuba player I told you about earlier, he actually bought one of those long black leather trench coats after we watched it in high school. He wore it every single day during senior year, even in May when it was like eighty degrees out. He sweat so much in that thing. He kept trying to convince everyone he was going to buy a motorcycle to match it, but his mom works at the county hospital and she calls them "donor-cycles," so she absolutely forbade it. She works in the cafeteria there, actually, and they make this incredible green jello with little chunks of pineapple in it. I don't even really like pineapple usually, it makes my tongue feel kind of scratchy and fuzzy, but in the jello it's perfect. 

But anyway, yeah, my supervisor shows me the normal entries on his green screen, but I still just feel like... I don't know, I still feel certain that they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. The numbers, I mean. It just feels too specific to be a coincidence.
Can you tell me more about how you know the invoice totals and account numbers are messages specifically for you? How did you come to understand that they are meant for you to read?

Well, it's hard to explain exactly *how* I know, it just... it just clicks in my head. Like I was saying, even when my supervisor literally sits there and shows me the original paperwork to prove they're just normal entries, it doesn't change anything. I still get totally convinced that they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. 

It's like a puzzle, you know? I used to be really obsessed with puzzles. My aunt bought me this massive 2,000-piece jigsaw puzzle of the Eiffel Tower for Christmas one year when I was in high school. It took up the entire dining room table for like three months. My mom was so annoyed because we had to eat dinner on the couch watching TV every single night until I finished it. We usually watched Jeopardy. Alex Trebek was still hosting back then, and he was always just so classy. He never made the contestants feel dumb, even when they guessed something completely ridiculous. 

I actually wanted to try out for the high school trivia team because I got so good at guessing the Jeopardy answers, but the tryouts were on the exact same day as my driver's ed final. I failed the parallel parking part of that test, actually. I bumped the orange cone, and the instructor—this older guy with a really thick mustache who always smelled like peppermint and stale coffee—he just sighed and wrote something down on his clipboard. I really hate clipboards. I feel like they just make people look intimidating for absolutely no reason, like they're judging you. My supervisor uses a clipboard sometimes when he does inventory, which is probably why I get so stressed out. But yeah, the invoice numbers and the due dates... I just feel certain they're testing me to see if I get the pattern.
Do you ever feel like the messages you're seeing in the invoice numbers or account details are part of a larger system watching or controlling you?

A larger system... yeah, I guess so. I mean, like I was saying before, it doesn't matter that my supervisor sits there and shows me they're just normal entries. I still get totally convinced that those specific invoice totals and due dates are messages about me. I just know they're tracking whether I understand the pattern. So yeah, it definitely feels like something bigger is watching me through the accounts. 

Which is kind of funny when you think about it, because our office network is so incredibly slow. The router is literally from like 2015. It has these two little antennas that make it look like it has rabbit ears. My grandpa used to have a TV with actual rabbit ears on top of it in his living room. You had to put tin foil on the ends of them just to get the baseball games to come in clear. He was completely obsessed with the Cubs. We'd sit out on his back porch in the summer and listen to the games on this tiny battery-powered radio he had. The batteries were always dying, so the announcer's voice would get all slow and distorted, like he was talking underwater. 

I tried holding my breath underwater for two minutes once in my neighbor's pool, but I only made it to forty-five seconds before I thought my chest was going to cave in. The chlorine in that pool was so strong, it actually bleached the tips of my hair. I looked like I was in a boy band for a month. 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, the accounts. Yeah, even with the normal entries, I definitely feel like they're tracking me to see if I get the pattern.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions or fixed false beliefs, which would help distinguish between schizophrenia (F20.6/F20.9) and other non-psychotic disorders (F23.9, F22.9).
doctor.question: Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn't seem to understand or agree with, even though you felt certain it was true?

target_item.name: Delusions

patient.answer:
Believed something strongly... yeah, actually. I know it sounds strange, but at work, I get completely convinced that certain invoice totals, or like, specific account numbers and due dates are actually messages about me. Like they're put there specifically for me to read. My supervisor will sit down with me and pull up the ledgers to show me they're just normal entries. He uses this really old accounting software, by the way, it's from like 2010 or something. The whole interface is just this depressing gray and neon green. It totally looks like the code falling in The Matrix, you know? Have you seen that movie? 

The first one is a classic, but the sequels get so confusing. My buddy Mark, the tuba player I told you about earlier, he actually bought one of those long black leather trench coats after we watched it in high school. He wore it every single day during senior year, even in May when it was like eighty degrees out. He sweat so much in that thing. He kept trying to convince everyone he was going to buy a motorcycle to match it, but his mom works at the county hospital and she calls them "donor-cycles," so she absolutely forbade it. She works in the cafeteria there, actually, and they make this incredible green jello with little chunks of pineapple in it. I don't even really like pineapple usually, it makes my tongue feel kind of scratchy and fuzzy, but in the jello it's perfect. 

But anyway, yeah, my supervisor shows me the normal entries on his green screen, but I still just feel like... I don't know, I still feel certain that they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. The numbers, I mean. It just feels too specific to be a coincidence.

inference.note: This turn added F20.6 (Schizophrenia, residual type) as a candidate due to the presence of auditory hallucinations and delusional thinking regarding messages in numbers. It did not rule out F20.9 (Schizophrenia, unspecified) or F23.9 (Acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms of schizophrenia) but supports F20.6 more strongly due to the chronic, delusional nature of the presentation rather than an acute, transient state. F22.9 (Persistent delusional disorder) is ruled out as the symptoms are broader than just delusions alone.

doctor.question: Can you tell me more about how you know the invoice totals and account numbers are messages specifically for you? How did you come to understand that they are meant for you to read?

target_item.name: Delusions

patient.answer:
Well, it's hard to explain exactly *how* I know, it just... it just clicks in my head. Like I was saying, even when my supervisor literally sits there and shows me the original paperwork to prove they're just normal entries, it doesn't change anything. I still get totally convinced that they are tracking whether I understand the pattern. 

It's like a puzzle, you know? I used to be really obsessed with puzzles. My aunt bought me this massive 2,000-piece jigsaw puzzle of the Eiffel Tower for Christmas one year when I was in high school. It took up the entire dining room table for like three months. My mom was so annoyed because we had to eat dinner on the couch watching TV every single night until I finished it. We usually watched Jeopardy. Alex Trebek was still hosting back then, and he was always just so classy. He never made the contestants feel dumb, even when they guessed something completely ridiculous. 

I actually wanted to try out for the high school trivia team because I got so good at guessing the Jeopardy answers, but the tryouts were on the exact same day as my driver's ed final. I failed the parallel parking part of that test, actually. I bumped the orange cone, and the instructor—this older guy with a really thick mustache who always smelled like peppermint and stale coffee—he just sighed and wrote something down on his clipboard. I really hate clipboards. I feel like they just make people look intimidating for absolutely no reason, like they're judging you. My supervisor uses a clipboard sometimes when he does inventory, which is probably why I get so stressed out. But yeah, the invoice numbers and the due dates... I just feel certain they're testing me to see if I get the pattern.

doctor.question: Do you ever feel like the messages you're seeing in the invoice numbers or account details are part of a larger system watching or controlling you?

patient.answer:
A larger system... yeah, I guess so. I mean, like I was saying before, it doesn't matter that my supervisor sits there and shows me they're just normal entries. I still get totally convinced that those specific invoice totals and due dates are messages about me. I just know they're tracking whether I understand the pattern. So yeah, it definitely feels like something bigger is watching me through the accounts. 

Which is kind of funny when you think about it, because our office network is so incredibly slow. The router is literally from like 2015. It has these two little antennas that make it look like it has rabbit ears. My grandpa used to have a TV with actual rabbit ears on top of it in his living room. You had to put tin foil on the ends of them just to get the baseball games to come in clear. He was completely obsessed with the Cubs. We'd sit out on his back porch in the summer and listen to the games on this tiny battery-powered radio he had. The batteries were always dying, so the announcer's voice would get all slow and distorted, like he was talking underwater. 

I tried holding my breath underwater for two minutes once in my neighbor's pool, but I only made it to forty-five seconds before I thought my chest was going to cave in. The chlorine in that pool was so strong, it actually bleached the tips of my hair. I looked like I was in a boy band for a month. 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, the accounts. Yeah, even with the normal entries, I definitely feel like they're tracking me to see if I get the pattern.
